name: Eleanor Whitcomb, Sacral Pressure Injury HD 3

caseMeta.title: Pressure Injury, Stage 3-4 Sacral - Hospital Day 3
learningObjectives: Stage and describe a pressure injury (size, depth, tissue type, drainage, periwound skin) and use the Braden scale to plan prevention.
Implement a 2-hour turning schedule, pressure-redistribution surface and moisture management, and premedicate for dressing changes and debridement.
Care for a debrided wound with negative pressure wound therapy (seal, canister, foam changes, alarms) and recognize infection and osteomyelitis.
Support nutrition for wound healing (high protein, vitamin C, zinc, refeeding labs) and teach caregivers; recognize neglect risk.
Connect assessment findings, labs and orders to prioritize nursing care.
Safely administer medications using the MAR and linked monitoring data.

orders.name: 2 g sodium, consistent carbohydrate, high calorie, high protein diet
orders.instructions: Protein at every meal and snack; assist with set-up and feeding, sit upright 90 degrees for meals, offer small frequent meals; high-protein oral supplement three times daily. Calorie count x 3 days. Aspiration precautions until swallow screen done. Modified for 2 g sodium, consistent carbohydrate, high calorie, high protein.

orders.name: Bed rest; reposition every 2 hours; avoid lying on the sacrum or trochanter
orders.instructions: Keep head of bed at or below 30 degrees except for meals (limits shear); 30-degree lateral tilt with wedges; heels floated. No sitting on the sacral wound.

orders.name: Up to chair for meals with pressure-redistribution cushion, maximum 1 hour, assist x2
orders.instructions: Use a lift sheet or mechanical lift (no dragging); limit sitting to 1 hour three times daily with a cushion; return to the low-air-loss bed; NPWT tubing secured. PT to progress.

orders.name: Support surface: low-air-loss mattress with microclimate control
orders.instructions: Set to patient weight; confirm inflation each shift; use only ONE layer of linen and a breathable underpad (no plastic-backed pads, extra sheets or briefs on the mattress). Chair: pressure-redistribution cushion. Do not use donut cushions.
nursingConsiderations: Check that the head of bed is at or below 30 degrees when not eating to limit shear.

orders.name: Turning and repositioning every 2 hours
orders.instructions: 30-degree lateral tilt alternating left, back-tilt (off the sacrum) and right using wedges; document position and skin check at each turn; use a lift sheet to avoid friction and shear; float heels with pillows lengthwise under the calves; check hips, ischium, ears and elbows for new redness.
nursingConsiderations: Never position directly on the sacral wound or a reddened area that does not blanch.
Premedicate before turns when pain is severe.

orders.name: Braden scale and head-to-toe skin assessment
orders.instructions: Score all six Braden categories (sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, friction/shear). Inspect sacrum, coccyx, heels, ischium, trochanters, occiput, ears, elbows and under devices. Report any new non-blanchable redness or open area.
nursingConsiderations: Braden 12 or less = high risk: continue every-2-hour turns and the specialty surface.

orders.name: Wound care sacral wound: saline cleanse, moist packing, foam border (until NPWT)
orders.instructions: Premedicate 30-60 minutes before. Cleanse with normal saline (no povidone, peroxide or hypochlorite); pack lightly, including undermined areas, with saline-moistened gauze; cover with a silicone foam border dressing; seal edges away from the anal cleft and change immediately if soiled with stool. Measure length x width x depth, undermining and tunnels weekly; describe tissue type, drainage, odor and periwound skin at each change.
nursingConsiderations: Do not pack tightly: pressure delays healing.
Report increasing pain, foul odor, spreading redness, exposed or rough bone, or crepitus.

orders.name: Negative pressure wound therapy (wound VAC) -125 mmHg continuous
orders.instructions: Maintain -125 mmHg continuous. Check seal, canister volume and tubing each shift; empty canister when full and record output. Foam changes every 48-72 hours by the WOC nurse/trained RN: count the foam pieces in and out, measure the wound, protect periwound skin. If therapy is off for more than 2 hours: remove the foam and apply a moist saline gauze dressing and call the provider/WOC nurse.
nursingConsiderations: Stop therapy and call the provider for bright red blood in the tubing or canister or a sudden increase in bloody output.
Seal over the gluteal cleft often leaks: re-check seal after each turn and after incontinence.
Premedicate before foam changes.

orders.name: Moisture and incontinence management
orders.frequency: Check every 2 hours and after each episode
orders.instructions: Clean urine and stool promptly with a pH-balanced no-rinse cleanser; pat dry (no rubbing); apply barrier ointment around (not in) the wound; one breathable absorbent underpad; external urinary catheter for output monitoring; scheduled toileting when able. Keep stool from reaching the wound or NPWT drape.
nursingConsiderations: Send C. difficile PCR if 3 or more liquid stools in 24 hours (on antibiotics).
Avoid indwelling catheter unless needed for severe wound contamination or end of life.

orders.name: Pain assessment and premedication before dressing changes and turning
orders.frequency: Every 4 hours and before each dressing change
orders.instructions: Use a verbal numeric scale or PAINAD if cognitively impaired. Give the PRN oral opioid and acetaminophen 30-60 minutes BEFORE dressing changes, debridement or NPWT changes; reassess after the procedure. Unrelieved pain delays mobility and healing.
nursingConsiderations: Watch for sedation, constipation, confusion and urinary retention with opioids in older adults.

orders.name: Infection and osteomyelitis watch
orders.instructions: Temperature, wound odor, drainage amount and color, periwound erythema (mark borders), warmth, induration and wound depth. Report fever, rising heart rate, new hypotension, increased drainage, bone that is exposed or rough, or crepitus. Stage 4 over bone has osteomyelitis risk: ESR/CRP trending, bone biopsy if MRI or probe suggests it.
nursingConsiderations: Sepsis recheck: new confusion, SBP below 100, RR above 22 or lactate above 2.

orders.name: Blood cultures x2
orders.frequency: Once, before the first antibiotic dose
orders.instructions: Two sets from separate sites.

orders.name: Wound culture: deep tissue at debridement
orders.instructions: Send deep tissue after debridement (not a surface swab) for aerobic and anaerobic culture.

orders.name: Phosphorus, magnesium and potassium daily for 3 days (refeeding risk)
orders.instructions: Malnourished patient starting nutrition: report phosphorus below 2.5, potassium below 3.5 or magnesium below 1.5.

orders.name: Albumin and prealbumin
orders.instructions: Nutrition markers; interpret with CRP because inflammation lowers both.

orders.name: Strict intake and output; calorie count x 3 days; daily bed-scale weight
orders.instructions: External catheter output measured; record meals as a percent eaten and supplement volume; same bed scale each morning. Goal urine output above 0.5 mL/kg/hr.

orders.name: Speech therapy swallow evaluation
orders.instructions: Sleepy, debilitated older adult with poor intake: evaluate swallowing and diet texture before relying on oral supplements.

orders.name: Physical therapy and occupational therapy evaluation
orders.instructions: Bed mobility, safe transfers with a mechanical lift, chair cushion positioning and sitting tolerance; caregiver training. Avoid friction and shear.

orders.name: Social work / case management: caregiver capacity, neglect screening, disposition
orders.instructions: A stage 3-4 pressure injury in a dependent adult needs an assessment of caregiver capacity and supplies; screen for neglect per policy and report concerns. Arrange SNF/home health, NPWT equipment, a pressure-redistribution mattress and wheelchair cushion, and wound clinic follow-up.

orders.name: Fall precautions (frailty, opioid, confusion)
orders.instructions: Bed low with alarm, call light in reach, assist x2 for transfers with lift, delirium prevention bundle (glasses, hearing aids, reorient, sleep protection).

orders.name: Point-of-care blood glucose
orders.instructions: Check before meals and at bedtime; every 6 hours while NPO. Treat per hypoglycemia protocol.

orders.name: Hypoglycemia protocol
orders.instructions: Follow facility hypoglycemia protocol: 15 g fast carbohydrate if awake, recheck in 15 minutes; dextrose 50% IV if NPO or unable to swallow.

orders.name: Daily weight
orders.instructions: Same scale each morning before breakfast; report gain of more than 2 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week.

orders.name: Delirium precautions and frequent reorientation
orders.instructions: Lights on by day, off at night; glasses/hearing aids; reorient often; avoid restraints; limit sedatives and anticholinergics.

orders.name: Fall precautions (bed alarm on)
orders.instructions: Bed alarm on, low bed, frequent rounding, toileting schedule.

orders.name: Dietitian consult: nutrition assessment
orders.instructions: Calorie counts x3 days; weekly weights; assess swallowing and dentition; start slowly (10-20 kcal/kg/day) and advance over 3-5 days.

orders.name: Refeeding syndrome precautions
orders.instructions: Check phosphorus, magnesium and potassium daily for 3 days after feeding starts; replace before they fall. Report HR irregularity, weakness, confusion, edema, respiratory difficulty.
nursingConsiderations: Phosphorus below 2.5 or K below 3.5: notify provider for replacement before advancing calories.

orders.name: Pressure injury prevention
orders.instructions: Braden score every shift; reposition every 2 hours, offload heels and sacrum, pressure-redistributing mattress.

orders.name: Scheduled toileting every 2 hours while awake
orders.instructions: Prompted voiding schedule, offer toileting before and after meals and at bedtime; commode at bedside; avoid indwelling catheter.

orders.name: Perineal skin care and moisture barrier
orders.instructions: Cleanse with pH-balanced cleanser, apply barrier cream; change briefs promptly; inspect for incontinence-associated dermatitis.

orders.name: Frailty precautions: falls, delirium and skin tears
orders.instructions: High fall risk (bed alarm, assist x1-2, scheduled toileting); delirium prevention (glasses/hearing aids, orientation, sleep, avoid sedatives); fragile skin: paper tape or silicone dressings, pad bony areas, no friction when repositioning.

orders.name: Dietitian consult and nutrition support
orders.instructions: Weight loss and low albumin: high-protein supplements between meals, feeding assistance, weekly weights.

orders.name: PT/OT evaluation and early mobilization
orders.instructions: Up to chair for meals, ambulate with assistance 3 times daily; evaluate for rehab placement.

orders.name: Goals of care and polypharmacy review
orders.instructions: Palliative/geriatrics input as needed; review code status and deprescribe where possible. Start low and go slow with new medications.

orders.name: Vital signs
orders.instructions: Notify provider for SBP below 90 or above 180, HR above 120 or below 50, RR above 28, SpO2 below 90%, or temperature above 101.5 F.

orders.name: Chest x-ray, portable
orders.instructions: Perform Chest x-ray, portable.
orders.rationale: Fever and sleepiness: evaluate for a pulmonary source

orders.name: Consult: Wound / Ostomy Nursing
orders.instructions: Stage 4 sacral pressure injury

orders.name: Consult: General Surgery (wound debridement)
orders.instructions: Infected stage 4 pressure injury with necrotic tissue

orders.name: Consult: Nutrition
orders.instructions: Malnutrition and pressure injury

orders.name: MRI pelvis (sacrum and coccyx) without contrast
orders.instructions: Perform MRI pelvis (sacrum and coccyx) without contrast.
orders.rationale: Stage 4 sacral pressure injury: evaluate for osteomyelitis

orders.name: CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP)
orders.instructions: Draw at 0500 daily. CBC plus CMP (sodium, potassium, chloride, CO2, BUN, creatinine, glucose, calcium, AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, albumin, total protein). Admission labs were drawn in the ED; the first routine AM draw is 2026-10-21 at 0500.

orders.name: Magnesium and phosphorus
orders.instructions: Draw with the 0500 labs. Replace per protocol (magnesium goal 2.0 or higher with arrhythmia risk).

orders.name: Platelet and kidney monitoring for heparin / low-molecular-weight heparin
orders.instructions: Platelets are checked every 2-3 days for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (a fall of 50% or to below 100); creatinine is checked because enoxaparin is cleared by the kidneys. Hold and call for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: Potassium and creatinine monitoring for diuretic / ACE inhibitor / ARB
orders.instructions: Report potassium below 3.5 or above 5.0, or a creatinine rise of 0.3 or more. Hold ACE inhibitor/ARB and call for SBP below 100 or rising creatinine/potassium.

orders.name: Vancomycin trough or AUC
orders.frequency: Before the 4th dose, then per pharmacy
orders.instructions: Draw 30 minutes before the dose. Pharmacy adjusts the dose; monitor creatinine daily.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale
orders.instructions: Administer Low-dose correction scale Subcutaneous ACHS (before meals and at bedtime).

medication.importantInfo: Give per correction scale only with a meal (or q6h if NPO). Check glucose first and document it. Watch for hypoglycemia.

orders.name: vancomycin IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 750 mg IV Every 24 hours. Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/hr, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.
orders.rationale: Empiric MRSA coverage until final culture
nursingConsiderations: Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/hr, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.

medication.importantInfo: Infuse over at least 90-120 minutes (no faster than 1 g/hr) to avoid vancomycin infusion reaction. Dosed by AUC (goal 400-600) or trough; extra caution in older adults and with dehydration or AKI. Monitor creatinine daily and urine output; report ringing in the ears. Stopped when the final culture shows no MRSA.
medication.hold: Hold and call pharmacy/provider for creatinine rise of 0.3 mg/dL or more, urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/hr, or vancomycin level above 20 mcg/mL.

orders.name: ascorbic acid (vitamin C) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mg Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Supports collagen synthesis in wound healing; usual course 10-14 days. High doses can cause kidney stones and loose stools.

orders.name: zinc sulfate capsule
orders.instructions: Administer 220 mg (50 mg elemental zinc) Oral Daily.
orders.rationale: Pressure injury healing / zinc deficiency risk

medication.importantInfo: Give with food (nausea). Limit to 10-14 days: prolonged use causes copper deficiency and anemia.

orders.name: multivitamin with minerals tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Part of the nutrition plan for wound healing.

orders.name: high-protein oral nutrition supplement (ENSURE ENLIVE)
orders.instructions: Administer 1 bottle (350 kcal, 20 g protein) Oral TID.

medication.importantInfo: Give between meals, chilled; sit upright and assist. Record the percent consumed. Hold if NPO.

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Check BP before giving. Monitor potassium and creatinine. Watch for cough and angioedema.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is below 100.

orders.name: carvedilol (COREG) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 6.25 mg Oral BID. Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

medication.importantInfo: Give with food. Check BP and HR before giving.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if HR below 55 or SBP below 100.

orders.name: furosemide (LASIX) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor BP, urine output, potassium, creatinine and weight.

orders.name: thiamine tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 100 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Give BEFORE starting nutrition or dextrose-containing fluids (refeeding / Wernicke prevention).

orders.name: multivitamin with minerals tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1 tablet Oral Daily.

orders.name: mirabegron (MYRBETRIQ) extended-release tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 25 mg Oral Daily. Hold and notify provider if SBP is above 180.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider if SBP is above 180.

medication.importantInfo: Swallow whole. Can raise blood pressure: check BP. Does not cause the confusion/dry mouth of anticholinergics.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider if SBP is above 180.

orders.name: oral nutrition supplement (ENSURE PLUS)
orders.instructions: Administer 8 oz (350 kcal) Oral BID.

medication.importantInfo: Give between meals, not with meals. Record percent consumed.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 650 mg Oral Every 6 hours.

medication.importantInfo: Scheduled; give 30-60 minutes before dressing changes and turning when possible. Maximum 3 g per 24 hours (2 g if malnourished or liver disease). Record temperature first.

orders.name: piperacillin-tazobactam (ZOSYN) IVPB
orders.instructions: Administer 3.375 g IV Every 8 hours.
orders.rationale: Infected pressure injury with sepsis (until 3-4 days after debridement)

medication.importantInfo: Covers E. coli, Enterococcus and anaerobes in an infected sacral wound. Extended infusion over 4 hours. Short course (about 4 days) after surgical debridement; the wound itself heals by debridement, nutrition and offloading, not by antibiotics. Watch for diarrhea (C. difficile) and rash.

orders.name: insulin glargine (LANTUS) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 20 units Subcutaneous Nightly at bedtime. Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes (home basal insulin, reduced 20% while NPO)
nursingConsiderations: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

medication.importantInfo: Basal insulin. Give even when NPO (dose reduced). Check glucose first; hold and call provider if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.
medication.hold: Notify provider before giving if glucose is below 100 mg/dL.

orders.name: donepezil (ARICEPT) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Oral Nightly at bedtime.

medication.importantInfo: May cause bradycardia, nausea, vivid dreams. Check HR before giving.

orders.name: enoxaparin (LOVENOX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Subcutaneous Daily. Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.
nursingConsiderations: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

medication.importantInfo: Monitor for bleeding, bruising, platelets and renal function. Never give if platelets below 50 or active bleeding.
medication.hold: Hold and notify provider for active bleeding or platelets below 50.

orders.name: tramadol (ULTRAM) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 25 mg Oral Every 6 hours PRN moderate pain (4-6). Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: Lowers seizure threshold; may cause dizziness and nausea.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10 or sedation.

orders.name: hydromorphone (DILAUDID) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 0.25 mg IV Every 3 hours PRN severe pain (7-10). Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.
nursingConsiderations: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

medication.importantInfo: HIGH-ALERT. Assess pain, sedation (RASS), RR and SpO2 before and 15-30 minutes after. Hold for RR below 10 or oversedation.
medication.hold: Hold for RR below 10, SpO2 below 90%, or sedation.

orders.name: zinc oxide 20% barrier ointment
orders.frequency: After each incontinence episode PRN skin protection after incontinence
orders.instructions: Administer Thin layer Topical After each incontinence episode PRN skin protection after incontinence.

medication.importantInfo: Cleanse with pH-balanced no-rinse cleanser and pat dry first. Apply to buttocks, perineum and skin folds but NOT into the sacral wound. Do not scrub.

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours PRN nausea or vomiting.

medication.importantInfo: Reassess nausea in 30 minutes. Check QTc in older adults before repeated dosing.

orders.name: lactated Ringer's bolus
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mL IV Once.
orders.rationale: Sepsis and dehydration (lactate 2.6, SBP 98); reassess lungs and BP after the bolus
nursingConsiderations: Stop the bolus and notify provider for new crackles, dyspnea or SpO2 drop.
